official_sources.title: GDAL Raster Data Model numeric precision limits
official_sources.finding: GDAL documents that some algorithms use 64-bit floating point internally and some paths can use 32-bit floating point; for UInt64/Int64 exact preservation through double-based paths is limited to about 2^53 or less, so large-integer raster values cannot be assumed exactly preserved after generic conversion/resampling.
official_sources.limitation: This establishes a numeric-integrity guard, not the target parcel elevation or the datatype of the eventual target DTM.

official_sources.title: GDALRasterBand raw nodata and scale-offset semantics
official_sources.finding: GDAL states nodata is reported as the raw stored value, decoded units equal raw*scale+offset, and RasterIO/ReadBlock do not automatically apply scale or offset.
official_sources.limitation: The actual target band still needs its own nodata, scale, offset and unit read from immutable source metadata.

official_sources.title: gdal_translate strict lossless conversion guard
official_sources.finding: gdal_translate strict mode is designed to fail instead of silently performing conversions that may lose information, including datatype conversions that cannot be exactly preserved.
official_sources.limitation: Strict behavior is driver-dependent and does not prove that any particular conversion is lossless without target-specific readback.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster edit mutable nodata scale and offset metadata
official_sources.finding: GDAL raster edit can assign nodata including NaN and infinities and can override scale and offset metadata, demonstrating that these interpretation fields are mutable and must be captured in immutable provenance.
official_sources.limitation: The edit command is an integrity-risk example; it is not a recommended transformation of the authoritative DTM.

official_sources.title: GDAL RFC 58 nodata representation hazards
official_sources.finding: GDAL RFC 58 records that an out-of-range nodata assignment can collapse to another representable value for narrow integer types and that losing a mask sidecar can expose hidden nodata semantics.
official_sources.limitation: The exact behavior depends on datatype and driver; target files must be inspected rather than assumed to exhibit this case.

official_sources.title: GDAL RFC 15 band mask validity semantics
official_sources.finding: GDAL formalizes raster validity masks as UInt8-like bands where zero means invalid/nodata and non-zero means valid, unifying explicit masks with nodata/alpha-derived validity.
official_sources.limitation: The actual target mask source and flags must be read from the target dataset and sidecars.

official_sources.title: GDAL VRT nodata remapping and hiding semantics
official_sources.finding: GDAL VRT can remap source nodata values and can hide a nodata value from readers, so VRT-derived bands can present different validity semantics from underlying sources unless source expressions are fully serialized.
official_sources.limitation: A VRT is derived metadata; it cannot silently replace immutable native raster evidence.

official_sources.title: NumPy finite-value classification
official_sources.finding: NumPy defines isfinite as the explicit element-wise test for values that are neither NaN nor positive/negative infinity.
official_sources.limitation: Finiteness is necessary but not sufficient; finite values can still be nodata, masked, out of range or incorrectly decoded.

official_sources.title: NumPy NaN classification semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy documents NaN as distinct from infinity under IEEE 754 and requires explicit isnan-style testing rather than ordinary equality.
official_sources.limitation: NaN policy must still be reconciled with the target raster's official nodata and mask semantics.

official_sources.title: NumPy floating-point machine limits
official_sources.finding: NumPy finfo exposes each floating datatype's bit width, epsilon, precision, range and subnormal behavior, making runtime numeric precision an auditable property instead of an implicit assumption.
official_sources.limitation: Machine limits describe representability, not survey accuracy or geospatial provenance.

official_sources.title: NumPy allclose tolerance semantics
official_sources.finding: NumPy allclose uses explicit absolute and relative tolerances, is not symmetric in rare cases, and warns that its default absolute tolerance can be inappropriate for values much smaller than one.
official_sources.limitation: Project acceptance must define domain-specific tolerances; default allclose settings are not evidence of exact equality.

official_sources.title: NumPy spacing and nextafter exact-neighbor tools
official_sources.finding: NumPy exposes nextafter and spacing for adjacent representable floating-point values and float-status indicators for overflow, underflow and invalid operations, supporting ULP-aware replay diagnostics.
official_sources.limitation: ULP diagnostics are QA tools; they must not loosen exact native-cell equality without an explicit project policy.

official_sources.title: NumPy nan_to_num replacement behavior
official_sources.finding: NumPy nan_to_num replaces NaN and infinities with finite values by default, so using it before extrema selection can fabricate apparently valid numeric candidates unless the replacement is explicitly prohibited or audited.
official_sources.limitation: This is a rejection guard; no such replacement is authorized for terminal elevation sampling.

official_sources.title: NumPy NaN-propagating versus NaN-ignoring extrema behavior
official_sources.finding: NumPy distinguishes NaN-propagating extrema operations from NaN-ignoring variants, so the chosen min/max primitive materially affects results when NaNs are present and must be explicit.
official_sources.limitation: NaN handling still cannot replace official nodata/mask filtering; raster validity semantics remain primary.
